UI_Meridian_Story1: <H1> DEPARTURE NOTICE <TEXT> Route M-01 remains open northeast. The city of Meridian guarantees shelter behind the wall. Bring fuel, food and a working radio. Do not leave the designated corridor. <LINE> <LINE> Someone has pencilled underneath: Why was this notice printed three months before the outbreak? <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 assembly: families wait beside the Last Light departure stores. The printed list promises every registered household a home; the handwritten revision removes four names. Keep the radio with the luggage, not in the lead vehicle.
UI_Meridian_Story2: <H1> ROADSIDE REGISTER <TEXT> Convoy 17 passed at 04:10. Civilian vehicles were sent east; Directorate vehicles continued northeast. The medical screening station was closed before the first civilian arrived. <LINE> <LINE> A folded map marks a supply cupboard behind the public counter. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 night stop: the quartermaster records a meal for sixty-three, but there are only sixty-one signatures. The missing family elected to wait for a relative. A child has drawn the same chest and field radio beside the next rest stop.
UI_Meridian_Story3: <H1> SCHOOL OFFICE MEMORANDUM <TEXT> All pupils completed the evacuation exercise. Attendance sheets must be forwarded to Population Continuity, not the school district. Parents are not to be told which pupils were assigned red wristbands.
UI_Meridian_Story4: <H1> WATER AUTHORITY REPORT <TEXT> The river samples are clean. The laboratory rejected our result and demanded the original sample bottles. Their security escort arrived before the report had been sent. <LINE> <LINE> Keep an independent sample. Hide it where the maintenance shelves meet the west wall. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 water diversion: the public direction board says continue straight, but the engineer orders a local service-road detour. A waterworks clerk keeps both versions of the order. Neither route requires restarting a pump.
UI_Meridian_Story5: <H1> CLINIC TRANSFER SHEET <TEXT> Patients presenting fever after screening are to be transferred north. No family visits. No local autopsies. Destination field: M-CONTINUITY. The doctor's last entry reads: They knew what symptoms to look for before we did.
UI_Meridian_Story6: <H1> RESERVOIR WORK ORDER <TEXT> The access road was widened for vehicles heavier than any municipal truck. Three sealed ventilation shafts were declared irrigation equipment. No water pipes lead to them. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 repair stop: the mechanics pooled tools, then left a damaged vehicle behind. The driver and two families transferred to other cars. Someone kept the original passenger list rather than the corrected Directorate copy.
UI_Meridian_Story7: <H1> CHECKPOINT DIRECTIVE <TEXT> Civilian settlements beyond this point are no longer on the resupply schedule. Retain fuel for Directorate transports only. Refugees must continue toward Meridian. The route is a collection system, not an escape route.
UI_Meridian_Story8: <H1> FIELD LABORATORY NOTE <TEXT> Exposure cohort C reached the checkpoint on schedule. The corridor's remaining clinics have been instructed to report only aggregate numbers. We are measuring migration under controlled scarcity. The wall is the last variable.
UI_Meridian_Story9: <H1> CAMP QUARTERMASTER'S LETTER <TEXT> We have ammunition for a war and medicine for a city, but orders forbid distribution. I have put a small reserve aside. If anyone outside the programme finds this: take what you need. Do not trust the screening gates. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 forest camp: a nurse describes an uneventful night, a shared meal and a family that turned back voluntarily. The official return lists them as missing. Not every absence is a death.
UI_Meridian_Story10: <H1> SUBLEVEL ACCESS RECORD <TEXT> Civilian housing above; emergency government below. Separate air systems. Separate food reserves. Separate lists of people worth saving. Every public building was designed with a service entrance to the network.
UI_Meridian_Story11: <H1> MERIDIAN EVACUATION BROADCAST <TEXT> All residents are to enter the underground refuge immediately. Surface patrols have withdrawn. Leave homes unlocked for emergency services. The broadcast repeats a recorded reassurance, although no operator remains at the console. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 screening list: admissions were based on employment category, not arrival order. Some relatives refused separation and stayed outside the closed zone. A clerk kept their names in a separate envelope.
UI_Meridian_Story12: <H1> REFUGE TRIAGE LOG <TEXT> Gate 4 admitted one patient without a final blood test. Clearance came from the Continuity Council. Six hours later the first housing sector stopped answering. Security sealed the lower doors with families still between them.
UI_Meridian_Story13: <H1> CONTINUITY COUNCIL: FINAL MINUTE <TEXT> The city was emptied into the safest place we had built. One infected person was enough. We planned the roads, the shortages, the screening and the destination. We did not plan for ourselves to be the last experiment. <LINE> <LINE> The surface is silent. The stores below remain full. <LINE> <LINE> Convoy 17 arrival reconciliation: forty-seven reached the surface homes. Some remained with the maintenance crew; others entered the refuge. The names missing from the underground register are not automatically casualties. The final household notes leave one returning family unaccounted for.
